title: macOS has no identity sources: SPEC promises Keychain and TouchID attestors that do not exist
description:
Measured on mark-mac, macOS 26.6.2, running a real personad built from a fresh clone of the public repo.

The daemon starts, binds, serves and fails closed. It also produces nothing:
  persona whoami     -> personad: no identity claims available
  persona fetch-jwt  -> error: personad: no identity claims available
  daemon log         -> event=svid_denied reason="no identity claims available"

probe_sources() reports count=1, and that one source is the OIDC cached attestor, which is the only attestor with no is_available() at all (persona-attestors/src/oidc.rs) and so registers unconditionally. Confirmed by elimination on that machine: SSH_AUTH_SOCK unset, no gpg binary, no /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock, and the count stayed 1 with SSH_AUTH_SOCK explicitly scrubbed. It then finds no token caches and yields no claims.

SPEC-HIA.md:725 and DESIGN.md:725 promise for macOS: 'Tailscale, Keychain, OIDC cached, SSH agent, GPG, DID, PIV' with 'TouchID (CryptoTokenKit), libfido2'. persona-attestors/src contains did_key, fido2, goa, gpg, oidc, piv, ssh, tailscale. There is no Keychain attestor and no TouchID/Secure Enclave attestor, on any platform. The two sources the docs single out as the macOS story are the two that were never written.

Of the attestors that do exist, on a stock Mac: goa is D-Bus/GNOME, tailscale probes a Linux socket path that the macOS GUI client does not create, gpg needs a binary that is not installed by default, fido2 and piv are feature-gated off.

Not a regression and not a crash. The daemon behaves correctly for a platform where nothing can attest -- it declines rather than fabricating, which is better than the Linux path does today (see .30, .49). The defect is that the documentation describes macOS support that does not exist.

Fix is either implementing a Keychain/TouchID attestor or correcting the two platform tables to say which sources are actually available today.
close_reason:
Decided by Mark 2026-09-15 (the platform tables describe the DESIGN, with every unbuilt item labelled) and applied in a84ff14 to README.md and SPEC-HIA.md. This extends the settled rule for unimplemented CLI commands to capability claims, which promise more than a command name does.

BEAD MEASUREMENT IS STALE. It was taken before the Unix account attestor existed. macOS is no longer mute: UnixAttestor carries no target_os gate and registry.rs adds it under cfg(unix), so a Mac now gets the OS account at iaa1 plus OIDC cached, SSH agent and GPG. 'probe_sources() reports count=1' and 'persona whoami -> no identity claims available' no longer hold.

What remains true and is now labelled: no Keychain and no TouchID/Secure Enclave attestor exists on any platform.

Checked against the code, not against the previous text, and several things were worse than the bead said:
- PIV: is_available() returns false in BOTH cfg arms, so it never activates even with --features pkcs11. The bead called it 'feature-gated off'; it is not implemented.
- GOA: the goa feature is a placeholder with no D-Bus dependency ('add zbus dep when implementing'), and is target_os = linux besides.
- FIDO2: real, but persona-attestors declares no default features, so it is compiled out unless --features fido2.
- Tailscale: hardcodes /var/run/tailscale/tailscaled.sock, so it never activates on macOS -- the bead had this right.
- did:web, KDE Wallet, WAM, PAM, Kerberos: no implementation anywhere; all were listed in SPEC-HIA's table on the same footing as shipped sources.
- Windows: personad does not run there at all.

The Linux row is measured rather than inferred: a real personad on this machine logged five active sources (tailscale, ssh-agent, oidc-cached, gpg, unix), with did:key skipped for an unset PERSONA_DID_KEYS. README now says which sources are unconditional (OIDC cached, Unix account) and which carry their own runtime check.

typos clean on both files.
